clue.text: In truth many will get covered with grease

indicators.note: the word for many is wrapped inside the word for grease, which covers it

parts.note: fat is grease, as in cooking fat
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: An assertion that a crowd of people will end up smeared in grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will get covered with' puts C inside FAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact is something true, so 'in fact' and 'in truth' are interchangeable phrases.

clue.text: Overweight got rid of with time, all due to a plant

parts.note: an overweight person is fat
to shed something is to get rid of it
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Losing weight over time is credited to some plant, perhaps a diet herb.
explanation.walkthrough: Fatshedera is a hybrid houseplant, a cross between fatsia and ivy (hedera).
explanation.definitionFit: Fatshedera is a hybrid evergreen shrub grown indoors, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Waterway preserve to which a fair number will go

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a fair-sized number

explanation.surface: A canal described as a place many people will visit to preserve it.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial channel for boats, a kind of waterway.

clue.text: 0 for a caring note!

explanation.surface: A zero offered as an affectionate message, like a kiss at the end of a card.
explanation.walkthrough: The figure 0 looks like the letter O, which in tennis scoring is love: so it is a letter meaning love.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol 0 is a letter standing for love (nil in tennis), and a note sent from the heart is a romantic missive.

clue.text: Bad order followed by one with good sense

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
I is the Roman numeral for one
nous is common sense or gumption

explanation.surface: A poor command is followed by somebody who shows sound judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, an honour given by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An ominous sign is a bad or threatening one, foreboding trouble.

clue.text: Egghead behind Oriental

indicators.note: the head of the word egg is its opening letter

parts.note: astern means behind, at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: An intellectual is lagging behind someone from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egghead' looks like one word for an intellectual, but it splits into 'Egg' and 'head': the head of egg gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe things from the East, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Beast making dash died

parts.note: dash in the sense of flair or verve is elan

explanation.surface: An animal that made a sudden run and then perished.
explanation.definitionFit: An eland is a large African antelope, a beast of the savannah.

clue.text: Will investigate before midday — before ten possibly

parts.note: to test is to investigate or try out
AM is the time before midday, so 'before midday' signals AM

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of ten may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A plan to examine something in the morning, maybe before ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before midday' is AM, the morning; 'possibly' rearranges TEN to ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament, as in last will and testament, is a legal document disposing of property.

clue.text: Spoke when called

definitions.meaning: a ladder's crosspiece, like a spoke of a wheel or chair
past participle of ring, as of someone telephoned

explanation.surface: Someone talked at the moment they were summoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder step or chair crossbar is a spoke-like bar, and someone telephoned has been phoned up, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Ringing about a boy worker

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a son is a boy
an ant is a worker, as in a worker ant

explanation.surface: Bells chime over a lad who is a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant sound is one that rings or echoes on.

clue.text: Operating in earnest where skin-treatment is provided

indicators.note: operating means working, so the letters are set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: A clinic working in earnest offering skin care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operating' rearranges the letters of IN EARNEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is a works where animal hides are cured into leather.

clue.text: Some popular songs give offence

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few chart hits cause offence.
explanation.walkthrough: Offence here is a crime, not hurt feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Everyone in the house gets a greeting

indicators.note: the word for everyone goes in the abbreviation for house

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
all means everyone

explanation.surface: The whole household is given a welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Hallo is an old-fashioned spelling of hello, used as a salutation.

clue.text: Too backward to incur debt

parts.note: over means too, as in overcautious

indicators.note: back placed before ward says the ward is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone too shy to go into debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' splits into 'back' and 'ward': 'back' turns WARD into DRAW.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdraw an account is to withdraw more than it holds, running into the red.

clue.text: Travellers may find it isn't near, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected new arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Wanderers may discover that their destination is further off than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges the letters of IT ISN'T NEAR (the apostrophe ignored).
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerants are people who move from place to place, so they are travellers.

clue.text: Deem ambiguous answer given is shaming

indicators.note: something ambiguous is open to more than one reading, so the letters are read in another order

explanation.surface: Judging an unclear reply is humiliating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ambiguous' rearranges DEEM to DEME.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to degrade or humiliate them.

clue.text: Learned people, and dedicated, but treated appallingly

parts.note: MAs are Masters of Arts, holders of a degree
sacred means dedicated, as to a god

explanation.surface: Scholars, devoted ones, are badly mistreated.
explanation.definitionFit: To massacre is to slaughter, or informally to defeat or treat with savage brutality.

clue.text: Most distinguished head in case

parts.note: nob is slang for the head
lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: The most eminent leader is kept in reserve just in case.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of a word meaning aristocratic or illustrious, so the most eminent.

clue.text: Fliers' accommodation with bars

parts.note: sounds like a hotel for travellers with a drinking bar, but the fliers are feathered and the bars are metal

explanation.surface: A hotel for air travellers with bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire enclosure that houses pet songbirds.

clue.text: New sort of toaster produced in Egypt

indicators.note: a new sort of something is a rearranged version of it

explanation.surface: An innovative toaster manufactured in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New sort of' rearranges TOASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosetta is a port town on the Nile delta, where the famous stone was found.

clue.text: Fatty is a dope to change!

indicators.note: to change says the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A fool needs to reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges IS A DOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose tissue is body fat, so the word means fatty.

clue.text: A strict person turned up and managed to hold it

indicators.note: turned means the word up faces the other way
the word for managed holds it inside

parts.note: to run something is to manage it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disciplinarian arrived and coped with the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses UP to PU; 'to hold' puts IT inside RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A puritan is someone with rigid moral or religious standards.

clue.text: The aristocracy want an attendant around always

indicators.note: around says the attendant's word goes about the word for always

parts.note: a page is an attendant, as at court
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Nobles constantly want a servant at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: EER is e'er, a poetic form of ever.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the body of peers, the nobility as a whole.

clue.text: She certainly created a row!

parts.note: made means created
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A woman who definitely kicked up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a quarrel, but it is a line, as of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeline is a woman's name, so it can stand for any female.

clue.text: Scoffed at in the evening

indicators.note: the word at sits in the poetic word for evening

parts.note: e'en is a poetic contraction of evening
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone was mocked at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' suggests mocking, but means gobbled; EEN is e'en, poetic for evening.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to eat it greedily, so scoffed food has been consumed.

clue.text: A disheartening device

parts.note: sounds like something that depresses you, but it literally removes the heart, as of an apple

explanation.surface: A gadget that makes people lose hope.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen tool that removes the central part of fruit, its heart.

clue.text: Dance that's unconventional to a degree!

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or unconventional
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A dance that is extremely eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a degree' looks like 'somewhat', but gives BA, a university degree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a ballroom dance of Cuban origin.

clue.text: A cold man can cause suffering

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A chilly man may bring on misery.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain, a kind of suffering.

clue.text: Keeping company with degenerate artist

parts.note: to rot is to decay or degenerate

explanation.surface: Associating with a decadent painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Corot was a nineteenth-century French landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot was a French painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Irish fruitarians?

parts.note: read literally as people eating citrus, but it points to the Protestant order in Ulster named after William of Orange

explanation.surface: Vegetarians from Ireland who live on fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The Orange Order is a Protestant fraternity, chiefly in Northern Ireland, named after King William III, William of Orange.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Loyal Orange Institution in Ireland bear a name that sounds like fruit-men.

clue.text: Finish up very annoyed when compromised

parts.note: to end is to finish up
angered means made very annoyed

explanation.surface: Someone ends up furious when put in a difficult position.
explanation.definitionFit: Something compromised or threatened is put at risk, the sense of in danger.

clue.text: The young woman left — the fool!

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: The girl walked out, the idiot!
explanation.definitionFit: A lass is a girl, a Scottish and northern English word.
